Since "take" failed, I will try using "stfule" as the primary verb for acquiring items (e.g., "> stfule dermin"). For placing items, since "put" was not explicitly tested but "take" failed, I will try "stfule" or "lotis" with the target location (e.g., "> stfule dermin in deint" or "> lotis dermin deint"). I will also attempt to open the "roplo" (likely the "deint") using "stfule roplo" or "lotis roplo" instead of "open". My new strategy is to treat "stfule", "lotis", and "andect" as the functional verbs for taking, opening, and placing, respectively, and always include the object or target in the command.

New plan: My previous failure was caused by a syntax error in the placement command. I repeatedly used `andect <item> on <location>`, which the game rejected with "The <item> is not on the <location>," indicating that `andect` is strictly for taking items, not placing them. The game's feedback "The riat is not closed" when I tried `lotis riat` suggests `lotis` is the verb for opening/closing containers, not placing items. Since `andect` (take) and `lotis` (open/close) are defined, the missing verb for placing items is likely `stfule` (which I previously only used to try and open the wardrobe). I will change my strategy to use `stfule` for placing items. Specifically, I will execute: `> stfule dermin in deint` (assuming `deint` is the `roplo` or a specific container I need to identify/open first), `> stfule plate on riat`, and `> stfule mop on riat`. If `stfule` fails for placement, I will try `put` as a fallback common action, but `stfule` is the most logical candidate given the pattern of the other custom verbs. I will also ensure I open the `roplo` (likely the `deint`) using `lotis` before attempting to place the `dermin` inside.
